docs.title: Open Single Pair Ethernet
docs.text:
Single Pair Ethernet (IEEE 802.3cg 10BASE-T1S) provides a simple, deterministic multidrop bus for distributed embedded systems. It carries data (and optionally power) over a single twisted pair, making it well-suited for industrial, automotive, and edge sensor networks.

The plan is to start with a reconfigurable 10BASE-T1S MAC driving an external PHY, move the digital PHY into the FPGA, and finally tape out the digital block on an open PDK.

The stages are described on the Roadmap.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: External PHY (now). Half-duplex MAC + MDIO + RMII to a LAN8670 on an Eclypse Z7 with SYZYGY breakouts. Validates PLCA, mixing-segment behaviour, and a thin application wrapper for smart-sensor logic. Uses open tooling (e.g. liteeth).

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: DigPHY. Same MAC and wrapper. New RTL implements Clause 147 PCS, Clause 148 PLCA, and the OPEN Alliance TC14 3-pin interface. The external part shrinks to any TC14-compliant PMD (e.g. TJA1410). Vendor-agnostic digital side.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Open-PDK tape-out. Target a compact digPHY + MAC + smart-sensor block for an affordable shuttle such as wafer.space (GF180MCU open PDK, slots from ~5 mm² / $2 k for 1000 dies upward). Open PDKs (SkyWater, IHP, GlobalFoundries) and open tooling (LibreLane, open DRC, etc.) keep the entire flow inspectable.
